title: add-capture-snapshotting-and-kernel-reconciliation-to-stabilize-replay-across-shape-perturbations
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: We observed intermittent warmup regressions when CUDA graph replays encounter small shape perturbations or partial KV-cache misalignment. Existing shape-guard heuristics either over-guard (preventing capture reuse) or under-guard (causing incorrect kernel replays). This PR implements a two-part runtime improvement: 1) persistent capture snapshots: lightweight, verifiable snapshots of the capture metadata (tensor shapes, stride hints, kernel signatures, KV cache root hashes) that can be persisted across ephemeral capture lifetimes and consulted during replay; 2) kernel reconciliation/stitching: a probe-driven reconciliation layer that attempts to reuse captured kernels by applying fast, safe transformations (axis-coercion, stride normalization, and small-kernel stitching) before falling back to full re-capture. Key design points: snapshots are compact (<=512B per capture) and opaque to backends; they include a TTL and monotonic version to avoid using stale captures after kernel migration. Reconciliation runs a prioritized sequence: (a) exact-match check, (b) stride/shape coercion with validation probe (dry-run on a small tile), (c) kernel-stitch attempt for fragmented batches (concatenate compatible kernel fragments), (d) safe fallback to non-graph execution or dynamic re-capture. Safety: every attempted reuse executes a validation probe which compares outputs on a small micro-batch under configured tolerances; if mismatch > epsilon or probe times out, the snapshot is retired and the request triggers re-capture. KV cache alignment: snapshot includes kv-root fingerprints allowing replay to fast-path only when prefix KV alignment is within bounds; otherwise reconciliation can realign keys for a limited window. Implementation: runtime/cudagraph/snapshot_manager.{h,cpp} manages lifecycle and persistence, runtime/cudagraph/reconciler.{h,cpp} implements probe logic and kernel-stitch primitives, scheduler/priming_coordinator.cpp integrates with continuous-batching to perform progressive priming using snapshots so common shapes receive validated captures earlier. Tests & validation: unit tests for snapshot serialization, reconciliation heuristics, and probe timeouts; integration tests that simulate shape jitter across batches; a synthetic perf harness measured P95 token latency and cold-start warmup times. Benchmarks: end-to-end text generation scenario with mixed sequence lengths (8/64/256 distribution) shows median P95 token latency improvement of ~18% across sustained load and a 60% reduction in observed warmup-induced latency spikes compared to baseline. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag cudagraph.snapshot_reuse; staged rollout: canary on dedicated pools -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on regression thresholds (3x error rate or 20% latency regression). Risk & mitigations: snapshot corruption detection causes safe retire & re-capture; reconciliation is deliberately conservative by default and can be made aggressive via tuning flags. Related work: follows ENG-3145 investigation into warmup flaps and complements prior shape-guard improvements by providing optimistic reuse with validation. Checklist: - [x] snapshot persistence and TTLs implemented - [x] reconciliation probe + kernel-stitch primitives - [x] KV fingerprinting and alignment checks - [x] unit/integration/perf tests - [x] feature-flag + rollout gating - [x] docs: runtime flags and observability metrics (cudagraph.snapshot.*)
commits: snapshots: add snapshot_manager and core serialization layer
reconciler: implement probe validation and kernel-stitching primitives
scheduler: wire priming coordinator to use snapshots during continuous batching
review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Nice approach to persist only metadata—did you consider including a versioned kernel ABI fingerprint to detect driver-level kernel mismatches?
Maya Patel: Good call. I added a kernel_abi_hash to the snapshot and a monotonic version field so we can invalidate snapshots on driver or kernel ABI upgrade.
Zara Novak: Probe wall-time could add latency on the hot path—can we amortize probes across the batch or run them on a small async tile?
Maya Patel: Probes run on a 16-token micro-batch inline but with a tight timeout; priming coordinator can run async priming for cold captures. Added config for probe_tile_size and probe_timeout.
Diego Ramos (requested changes): please add integration tests that simulate KV misalignment across interleaved requests and assert snapshot retirement logic.
Maya Patel: Added tests/integration/cudagraph_kv_misalignment.test and extended the shape_jitter test to include KV permutations. Ready for final review.
Ethan Brooks: Approving — results look good on canary, no regressions observed in nightly perf runs.
release_notes: Introduce persistent CUDA-graph capture snapshots to enable safe replay across small shape perturbations.
Add probe-driven kernel reconciliation and stitching to increase capture reuse without sacrificing correctness.
KV-cache fingerprinting enables safe fast-path reuse when prefix alignment is preserved.
Feature-gated and rolled out gradually with observability exposed under cudagraph.snapshot.* metrics.
notes: Observability: added metrics cudagraph.snapshot.used, cudagraph.snapshot.retired, cudagraph.reconcile.probe_latency and a debug log level for reconciliation decisions. Ops: can disable snapshot reuse per pool via pool config. Performance: measured safe reductions in warmup flaps during mixed-sequence traffic.
